Yes, the story has an appropriate balance between scene and summary/exposition. 

Because the narrative spans roughly half a year (from autumn through April), it effectively uses summary and exposition to compress time, provide background on the university's bureaucratic history, and show the gradual wearing down of the staff (such as summarizing how each staff member adapted their routines by winter). At the same time, it anchors every section with brief, vivid scenes in real-time—complete with snappy dialogue and specific actions, like the emergency meeting, Miriam's conversation with Noor about office space, Danny standing ankle-deep in the flooded stairwell, and Miriam's dinner with her husband. This interplay keeps the pacing brisk while ensuring the characters and their frustrations feel immediate and engaging.
